article_title: When Imagination Runs Dry: Disney's IP Overload
news_headline: Disney Cutting Hundreds More Jobs in New Round of Corporate Streamlining
post_text: Disney has now run three separate rounds of layoffs in 2026 under new CEO Josh D'Amaro, cutting hundreds of jobs across Pixar, ESPN, National Geographic, and its broader corporate functions. The latest restructuring, branded "One Disney," consolidates the company's television operations away from legacy linear brands and toward a unified streaming structure. Pixar absorbed some of the deepest studio cuts, a notable detail given that the studio's last two releases, an original film and Toy Story 5, were among Disney's bigger bets this year. The pattern here goes beyond cost management. When a studio keeps returning to sequels and sequels of sequels, the creative pipeline thins, and the organizational costs of propping up those franchises eventually compound. WBR's piece on Disney's IP overload argued exactly this: that the reliance on recycled franchises carries a structural price that doesn't show up until it does. That bill is now being itemized.
